prompt_feedback: Community Notes are not available through the X API here: post.fields community_notes is rejected, so doubt levels this run come from replies and quote posts only, with no browser check.

Saves are read from the Twitter Profile archive on the box (/workspace/x-ai-bookmarks/bookmarks_ai.jsonl and discarded.jsonl), not from the X plugin bookmarks call; the prompt should say so and name the captured_at field for the time window.

The archive fields (id, url, text, created_at, author_username, links, github_repos, category, reason, first_seen_at, captured_at, posted_at) differ from what the prompt implies; 97 backfill records share one captured_at near 2026-10-14T04:4xZ, so captured_at plus posted_at is needed to find new saves.

Every X read returns at most 25 results even when 50 or 100 is requested, so one query per group does not cover 24 hours for busy groups; the builders group needed 4 pages and still left a gap of about 1.6 hours near 2026-10-20T09:06Z.
get_posts_quoted_posts returns plain reposts unless exclude retweets,replies is passed; the prompt should specify that.
The min_likes search operator appears to be ignored by search_posts_all, so discovery queries return mostly low-engagement posts.
Video analysis needs a video-capable reader; this run only downloaded 3 clips over 60 seconds for later analysis and left the video field out of items.

config/scout.json has follow_mode browser, but runs so far have no browser and are told to report follow candidates to the parent instead of following or logging; through the 18:10Z sweep no account has 3 qualifying sweep-file posts yet.

search_posts_all returns a next_token even when result_count is below max_results; following it for a 30-minute window returned nothing, so treat result_count under max_results as the end of the window and skip the extra page.
Post public_metrics come back as repost_count, not retweet_count; the prompt's metrics.reposts should map from repost_count.

TorchTPU (announced around 11:30Z by Google Cloud accounts) only reached the sweep through a later @PyTorch post; @googlecloud, @GoogleOSS or a Google Cloud Tech account may be worth a roster review look.
